summary: Background: Shengyu decoction (SYD) is a classic and excellent prescription of traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM). summary: Transcriptomic analysis on SHR chondrocytes supported enhanced glycolysis and aberrant mTOR signalling. During chondrocyte development, we identified IGF2 as one of the most significantly downregulated genes in WKY, while genes involved in rheumatoid arthritis and glycolysis were prominently enriched in SHR.

title: Transcriptomic profiling of DHA-treated human chondrocytes
summary: This study aimed to investigate the regulatory effects of docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) on lipid metabolism in human osteoarthritic chondrocytes. All cells were pretreated with 10 ng/mL interleukin-1β (IL-1β) for 24 hours to simulate the inflammatory environment of osteoarthritis. Subsequently, cells were divided into two groups: one treated with 25 μM DHA for 48 hours and the other with PBS as control. Total RNA was extracted and subjected to strand-specific paired-end RNA sequencing to examine transcriptomic changes related to lipid metabolic pathways.

title: Osteocyte-specific deletion of Gasdermin D drives osteoarthritis cartilage degeneration by promoting inflammation and remodeling in subchondral bone
summary: In osteoarthritis, we discovered that the number of osteocytes in the subchondral bone is reduced. By investigating the interaction between chondrocytes and osteocytes, we aim to elucidate the underlying pathological mechanisms.

summary: Chondrodysplasia is a genetic disorder characterized by impaired cartilage development and bone growth. summary: Osteoarthritis (OA) is typically characterized by progressive cartilage breakdown, subchondral bone remodeling, osteophyte formation and low-grade joint inflammation. Accumulative evidence demonstrates that cartilage fibrosis and the resulting degradation of extracellular matrix are implicated in the late-stage pathology of OA. summary: This study investigates the role of chondrocyte heterogeneity in osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) through single-cell RNA sequencing of 50,851 chondrocytes from 10 ONFH patients and 10 controls.

summary: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS), the spontaneous development of a lateral spine curvature during puberty, is the most common pediatric spine disorder, affecting ~3% of children worldwide. summary: Precise spatiotemporal regulation of parathyroid hormone (PTH) and PTH-related peptide (PTHrP) signaling through the PTH1R is fundamental to skeletal development and metabolic bone remodeling, yet the intracellular mechanisms that fine-tune this signaling remain a central unanswered question. summary: Cartilage is characterized by a highly specialized extracellular matrix (ECM) secreted by chondrocytes and limited self-regenerative capacity. In vivo investigations of chondrogenesis are limited by difficult and traumatic access, especially in humans. While it is known for decades that disturbances of chondrocyte differentiation and changed cartilage ECM composition cause severe phenotypes skeletal phenotypes in vertebrates, a detailed molecular understanding of chondrogenesis and cartilage ECM formation is still missing, especially in the context of human genetic skeletal diseases.

title: Single-cell RNA sequencing of chondrocytes from osteoarthritis (OA) patients and healthy controls
summary: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage degeneration and osteophyte formation. summary: This study proposes a strategy to alleviate cellular hypoxia using platelet membrane-coated nanothylakoid units (NTU@PM), taking advantage of their light-driven oxygen-generating capacity. Transcriptomic analysis was performed to investigate their effects on hypoxic mouse macrophages.

title: Reprogramming Dedifferentiation Regulatory Networks Preserves Human Chondrocyte Phenotypes (RNA-Seq)
summary: Chondrocyte-based cartilage repair strategies such as autologous chondrocyte implantation (ACI) require extensive in vitro expansion to obtain clinically relevant cell numbers. However, monolayer expansion drives chondrocyte dedifferentiation, reducing matrix-forming capacity and contributing to variable repair outcomes, a long-standing problem in cell-based cartilage repair.

title: Dermal fibroblasts attenuate osteoarthritis by restoring synovial fibroblast homeostasis
summary: Background: Managing early-to-mid-stage knee osteoarthritis (OA) remains an unmet clinical need. title: Sturgeon Cartilage–Derived Peptides Promote Cartilage Repair-Associated Responses in Osteoarthritis via Integrin αvβ3–PI3K/Akt Signaling
summary: Osteoarthritis (OA) features progressive cartilage loss with no effective regenerative therapies. This study investigated sturgeon cartilage peptides (SCPs) for OA repair and identified key bioactive peptides and mechanisms. SCPs, prepared by trypsin hydrolysis, were evaluated in in vitro and in vivo OA models. SCPs markedly improved cartilage damage, reduced matrix degradation, and increased chondrocyte proliferation to 126%.

title: The transcription factors SOX9 and SOX5/SOX6 cooperate genome-wide through super-enhancers to drive chondrogenesis (RNA-Seq)
summary: SOX9 is a transcriptional activator required for chondrogenesis, and SOX5 and SOX6 are closely related DNA-binding proteins that critically enhance its function. summary: This research was designed to determine why fetal chondrocytes evidence regenerative capacity and adult chondrocytes do not. We then also compared adult chondrocytes treated with a newly discovered small molecule agonist of gp130 to those that weren't treated.
